meta.title: Usage
meta.description: A complete React Scheduler example, how controlled and uncontrolled state work, and the props most applications set first.

demos.minimal: Items, a day, and nothing else

minimal.intro: Three props carry a working schedule: the items, the day to show, and the language pack. Everything else has a default. Open the source below the demo to see the whole file — it is the file that runs on this page.

controlled.intro: Every piece of state the component keeps has an uncontrolled form, where the component owns it and only reports changes, and a controlled form, where your application owns it. Uncontrolled is the default: pass the initial value with a default prop and forget about it.
controlled.controlled: Pass the value itself and the component stops owning it. From then on it renders what you give it and calls you on every change, so the value and the view can never drift apart.
points: view / defaultView with onViewChange — the list or the timeline.
openItemId / defaultOpenItemId with onOpenItemIdChange — which item's detail is open.
headerExpanded / defaultHeaderExpanded with onHeaderExpandedChange — the state of your own page header.
openOverflowId, overflowPage and overflowSort, each with its default form and its callback — the overflow dialog.

common.intro: The props most applications set. Every one of them is documented in full on the <link to="/api/scheduler/">Scheduler</link> page.
rows: The schedule itself: a flat array of items with an id, a start, a level and a title.
The day to show. The shifts that contain it are the ones rendered.
How the day is cut into shifts: a regular length and an anchor, or a named pattern. See <link to="/shifts-and-dates/">Shifts and dates</link>.
The severity scale: the ranks, their colors and which of them pin. See <link to="/items-and-levels/">Items and levels</link>.
'list' or 'timeline'. The reader can switch, unless you control it.
A locale pack. Seven are built in; the object is plain, so a partial override is enough.
Called when a reader opens an item, with the item and what activated it.
